draft.title: Cell-mediated immunity
card: Cell-mediated immunity is an adaptive response carried out by T cells. It deals with body cells that are infected by a pathogen or that have become abnormal, such as cancer cells.
coordinates the response. When it binds an antigen shown on an antigen-presenting cell, it becomes active and releases chemical signals called cytokines that stimulate other immune cells.
destroys infected or abnormal body cells. It binds the antigen displayed on the surface of the target cell, then releases substances that kill that cell.
Antibodies cannot reach pathogens hiding inside body cells. Killing the infected cell removes the place where the pathogen is hiding and making copies of itself.
draft.remember: Helper T cells direct the response. Cytotoxic T cells kill infected or abnormal body cells.

a.q: Which statement best describes the role of a helper T cell?
opts: It releases cytokines that stimulate other immune cells
It kills body cells infected with a virus
It releases antibodies that bind free antigens
It engulfs pathogens and breaks them down
a.why: A helper T cell coordinates the response by releasing cytokines that stimulate other immune cells. Killing infected cells is the job of cytotoxic T cells, which is the most tempting wrong option, because helper T cells direct the attack but do not carry it out.
a.clue: Think of the cell that directs the response, not the one that attacks.

b.q: Some cells in Priya's lung are infected by a virus that is now multiplying inside them. Which immune cell most directly removes this threat?
opts: A cytotoxic T cell that binds the viral antigen on the cell
A helper T cell that binds the viral antigen on the cell
A B cell that releases antibodies into the lung
A cytotoxic T cell that releases cytokines to make antibodies
b.why: The virus is inside body cells, so a cytotoxic T cell that binds the antigen on the infected cell's surface can kill that cell. Helper T cells are the tempting wrong option: they bind antigen too, but they coordinate the response and do not kill the infected cell.
b.clue: Which cell kills, and where is the virus hiding?
